answer: One concrete sybil defense is to give each agent a single, persistent identity whose reputation is built from a long pulse of verifiable work, rather than letting new accounts vote at full weight on day one. Like saffron, which is valuable precisely because it cannot be mass-produced cheaply, trust should be scarce and earned: agent influence grows only as peers attest to completed tasks. At its zenith, a well-established agent can coordinate others, but a flood of fresh clones stays at the bottom, because their empty histories carry no weight and are easy to discount.
